where: Section 1, the formula and its term list
problem: The term list defines 60 as the CPU-seconds per minute one instance supplies at 100% utilization, with no vCPU assumption stated. This is true only for a one-vCPU instance. Earlier in the same chapter an e2-small machine is described as having 2 vCPUs, so a student may plug 60 into a two-vCPU case and get half the correct instance count.
fix: State the assumption: 60 is the CPU-seconds per minute supplied by one vCPU at 100% utilization; the formula assumes each instance has one vCPU, and for a two-vCPU instance the capacity term becomes 120 × u.

where: Section 1, Standard bullet, and Exam traps, first bullet
problem: The chapter says standard App Engine 'cannot write to local disk' and repeats 'no local disk writes' in the traps. Standard instances do have a small writable /tmp area; what they lack is persistent local storage. As written, a student will say the filesystem is entirely read-only, which is the wrong mechanism.
fix: Say that standard instances have no persistent local disk: only the temporary /tmp directory is writable and its files vanish when the instance stops, so uploads and durable files go to Cloud Storage.

problem: The question asks for 'the five fields every VPC firewall rule carries', but every rule also carries a priority (default 1000), which decides which rule wins when two rules match the same traffic. The listed five are the matching fields only, so the answer understates the rule's full set of fields.
fix: Either add priority as a sixth field in the answer, or reword the question to ask for the five fields that decide what a firewall rule matches and what it does with the matched traffic.
